POE Clearance 
Q: What is "Emigration Clearance" and who needs it?  
A: Emigration Clearance is a legal requirement under the Emigration 
Act, 1983. It is mandatory for Indian passport holders in the ECR 
(Emigration Check Required) category who are traveling to specific 
countries for employment. 
Q: Which countries require me to get POE clearance before I 
fly for work?  
A: Currently, there are 18 countries where clearance is required for 
ECR passport holders: 
• 
Middle East: UAE, Saudi Arabia (KSA), Qatar, Oman, Kuwait, 
Bahrain, Jordan, Yemen, Syria, Lebanon, Iraq, Iran. 
• 
Africa: Libya, Sudan. 
• 
Asia: Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Afghanistan. 
Q: Is it true that I cannot travel to Iraq for work? 
A: Yes, currently emigration to Iraq is banned. Even for those with 
ECNR passports, traveling to Iraq for work usually requires special 
government clearance or is restricted due to security concerns. 
Q: How do I know if my passport is "ECR" or "ECNR"?  
A: Look at the last page of your passport. 
• 
If it has an endorsement saying “Emigration Check Required,” 
you are in the ECR category. 
• 
If there is no such endorsement, or if it explicitly says "ECNR" 
(or refers to the holder as being in a non-ECR category), you do 
not need POE clearance for travel. 
Q: I have an ECR passport, but I'm just going to the UAE for a 
10-day holiday. Do I still need clearance?
A: No. Since October 1st, 2007, ECR passport holders traveling for 
purposes other than employment (like tourism, visiting family, or 
study) do not need POE clearance. You simply need your valid 
passport, a valid visa, and a return ticket to show at the immigration 
counter. 
Q: Are there any professional groups that always need 
clearance, regardless of their passport status?  
A: Yes. Even if you have an ECNR passport, you must obtain POE 
clearance if you fall into these specific categories and are traveling to 
any of the 18 ECR countries: 
• 
Nurses traveling for work. 
• 
Seafarers traveling to join a vessel abroad. 
• 
Anyone traveling to Iraq (due to the current restrictions). 
Q: Can I apply for this clearance online?  
A: Yes. As of 2026, the process is fully digital through the eMigrate 
portal. You will need to upload your employment contract, your visa, 
and proof of your PBBY (Pravasi Bhartiya Bima Yojana) insurance. 
SEAFARERS AND E-MIGRATE 
Q: What is the e-Migrate system for seafarers?  
A: The e-Migrate system is a mandatory digital platform launched by 
the Directorate General of Shipping (DGS). It is designed to track and 
protect Indian seafarers, particularly those recruited for foreign-
flagged vessels. 
Q: Why was this system introduced?  
A: It was created to prevent seafarers from being exploited by 
unlicensed Recruitment & Placement Services (RPS). By using e-
Migrate, the government ensures that every seafarer is placed 
through a legitimate agency and has a valid contract. 
Q: Who is required to go through the e-Migrate process?  
A: Every Indian seafarer leaving an Indian seaport or airport to join 
a ship—regardless of rank—must be cleared through the e-Migrate 
system.
Q: What happens if I try to join a ship without e-Migrate 
clearance?  
A: You will not be allowed to board your vessel or continue your 
service. Immigration authorities at airports and seaports strictly 
verify e-Migrate status before allowing seafarers to depart. 
Q: Are there any exemptions to this rule?  
A: Generally, no, unless specifically exempted by the DGS guidelines 
(such as certain specialized personnel who are not categorized as 
"seafarers" under the Maritime Labour Convention). However, for the 
vast majority of active crew members, it is a mandatory requirement. 
Q: I am traveling through Mumbai Airport. Is there help 
available for this?  
A: Yes. As of 2026, there is a 24/7 Seafarers Facilitation Counter at 
Terminal 2 (Mumbai Airport). They can assist with document 
verification and help resolve any e-Migrate issues before you reach 
immigration. 
Q: Where can I find more details or check my e-Migrate 
status?  
A: You should visit the official website of the Directorate General of 
Shipping at www.dgshipping.gov.in. You can also manage your profile 
through the updated e-Samudra portal, which handles seafarer data 
as of 2026.

Ans: ETA is an Electronic Travel Authorization. It allows the bearer 
access into the issuing country (India). ETA is NOT eVisa. When the 
bearer of ETA is allowed entry into India by the Immigration Officer, 
it becomes eVisa. eVisa will be stamped on the Passport of the 
foreigner at the designated ICPs on production of valid ETA.

Expiry Date”?

India. Visa Expiry Date is the last date permitted for the stay of 
foreigner in India subjected to any stay stipulation applicable.
